summary.headline: Yasho Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 308 crore (volume +42% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 24.2%; management guides to sustain margins.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record Rs 308 crore, driven by 42% YoY volume growth from customer approvals and additional offtake in industrial chemicals. EBITDA rose to Rs 74.42 crore (24.2% margin, vs 17% previously cited), with PAT of Rs 36 crore (11.7% margin). Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.86x from 3.75x at Q4 FY26, bank loan ratings were upgraded to A- by CRISIL and ICRA, and working capital cycle shortened from 190 to 143 days. Management raised FY27 capex from Rs 125 crore to Rs 250 crore for two new buildings at Pakhajan and set a FY28 revenue target above Rs 1,600 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly revenue; 60% YoY growth per analyst question (not disputed)
From 3.75x at end of Q4 FY26

segments.name: Industrial chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 89% of Q1 revenue; management expects this to rise to about 90% going forward. Management said new-product revenue is about 30% of sales over the last two years, with revenue rising from Rs 600 crore to Rs 850 crore.

segments.name: Exports / geographies
segments.commentary: Export is about 69% of revenue; US sales recovered after tariff issues eased, and Europe and Middle East are growing. Asia and Africa are early-stage, with margins described as at par or slightly lower than US/Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained, given the Q1 benefit from the April price revision and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gains to product mix and higher utilisation rather than stock gains, citing commitments from marquee customers to maintain margins.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to move EBITDA margin from the historical 17-20% range to about 24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher utilisation (about 50% to 65%), higher customer offtake, product mix, and R&D-led process optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing and revenue potential of the Pakhajan capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 about Rs 100 crore and Phase 2 about Rs 150 crore, at about 2.5x asset turn. Management said the Rs 1,600 crore FY28 guidance excludes these buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain or raw material risks given the current macro environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a genuine raw material supply issue, and export container bookings can take three to four weeks. Inventory fell, which drove working capital down.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differential between new and old products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products earn about 10-12% higher margin than older products. Newly launched products in the last 12 months carry better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Lube-additive and ICE exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see EV adoption as a threat within a 10-year horizon, and that Rs 250 crore capex is not for lube alone.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to sustain the current EBITDA margin (about 24%) in FY27, though it said it cannot promise this beyond the next two to three years.
FY28 revenue target revised to more than Rs 1,600 crore; management said real growth from the new capacity comes from FY29.
Targets 30% to 40% annual revenue growth over the next few years.
FY27 capex raised to Rs 250 crore from Rs 125 crore; company expects about Rs 100 crore of borrowings in FY27.
Long-term agreement commercialisation expected in Q1 FY28, on track.
capex_capacity: Two new production buildings at Pakhajan facility for industrial chemicals, including new molecules and capacity for existing products. Phase 1 is about Rs 100 crore (operational Q1 FY28); Phase 2 is about Rs 150 crore (operational Q4 FY28). Management said the build takes at least 15 months.
Management expects about 2.5x asset turn on the Rs 250 crore capex.
Utilisation at the company level improved to over 65% (60-65% per another answer); management targets 70-75% and expects to add capacity once utilisation crosses 60-65%.
Management said about 60-65% of the new capacity is already covered by customer commitments.
Vapi plant shut; efforts moved to Pakhajan, which also has a pilot facility for R&D.
demand_pricing: Pricing is formula-based on raw material costs, reset quarterly or half-yearly, and management said long-term/contract business rose to more than 50% of revenue from 30-40% earlier.
Top customer is about 7% of revenue.
Management said the 42% volume growth reflects offtake, not pre-emptive buying; it expects volumes to grow sequentially.
Company is seeing more export traction than domestic; domestic sales are growing slowly.
Management cites a Rs 12-15 billion addressable market and an aspiration of $200-300 million revenue.
risks_watch: Raw material supply tightness and export container availability could affect output; management referenced a "war situation" in the macro backdrop.
Margin sustainability: management stated it wants to maintain margins for two to three years but cannot promise them.
Capex execution: Phase 1 and Phase 2 timelines depend on construction and commissioning within about 15 months.
Chinese capacity additions could pressure realisations; management did not give a direct answer.
Delivery times reportedly unchanged at 8-10 weeks higher than before (per analyst question).
key_quotes: The company achieved its highest quarterly revenue of Rs. 308 crores driven by a 42% increase in volume on a year-on-year basis.
Based on the current outlook, the company will endeavor to maintain current margins going forward.
We are not aiming immediately to go to $0.5 billion - $1 billion revenue. We are just talking about $200-$300 million revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term margins and growth, but evasive on specifics: declined to split Pakhajan-level utilisation, customer names, and Chinese competition, and repeatedly referred back to company-level metrics.

adds.what: Pakhajan Phase 1 new production building, industrial chemicals (new molecules and existing products), ~Rs 100 crore
Pakhajan Phase 2 new production building, industrial chemicals, ~Rs 150 crore

growth.why: Management targets 30-40% annual revenue growth and FY28 revenue above Rs 1,600 crore, backed by Pakhajan Phase 1 (~Rs 100 crore, operational Q1 FY28) and Phase 2 (~Rs 150 crore, Q4 FY28), with 60-65% of new capacity already covered by customer commitments; utilisation is above 65% with a 70-75% target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides to hold the ~24% EBITDA margin (up from 17-20% historically) through FY27, citing utilisation of 50% to 65%, product mix, and new products earning 10-12% higher margins, but the margin is not guaranteed beyond that.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY28 (Phase 1, ~Rs 100 cr); Q4 FY28 (Phase 2, ~Rs 150 cr)
rows.why: Two Pakhajan production buildings are under construction with Phase 1 operational Q1 FY28 and Phase 2 Q4 FY28; the build takes at least 15 months and 60-65% of new capacity is already covered by customer commitments.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 30-40% annual revenue growth and expects sequential volume growth; Q1 volume was up 42% YoY and utilisation rose to over 65% against a 70-75% target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex was raised from Rs 125 cr to Rs 250 cr for the Pakhajan buildings, with about Rs 18.73 cr spent in Q1 and about Rs 100 cr of borrowings expected in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY28 revenue target was revised up to above Rs 1,600 cr and 30-40% annual growth is targeted, but Q1 revenue of Rs 308 cr only supports this if volumes keep compounding and new capacity comes on stream from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management called raw material supply a genuine issue, export container bookings take 3-4 weeks, and delivery times are 8-10 weeks; the EBITDA margin of about 24% is guided for FY27 only, with management saying it cannot promise beyond 2-3 years.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New-product revenue is about 30% of sales over two years, Pakhajan Phase 1 carries new molecules, and the long-term agreement commercialisation is expected in Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Customer commitments cover new capacity
rows.why: Management said 60-65% of the new Pakhajan capacity is already covered by customer commitments, and long-term/contract business rose to over 50% of revenue from 30-40% earlier.

rows.label: Net debt/EBITDA down to 1.86x
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA fell from 3.75x to 1.86x and working capital days fell from 190 to 143, while FY27 borrowings of about Rs 100 cr are expected against the Rs 250 cr capex.

rows.label: Export growth in Europe, Middle East, Asia and Africa
rows.why: Exports are about 69% of revenue, US sales recovered after tariff issues eased, and Europe and Middle East are growing while domestic revenue grows only about 10% YoY.

tone.note: Management was confident on near-term margins (~24% held for FY27), volume growth and the Pakhajan build, but evasive on Pakhajan-level utilisation, customer names and Chinese competition; analysts pushed on margin sustainability and whether the April price revision drove Q1.
